inputs.wacc_rationale: JPY-denominated flows discounted at a JPY-built rate: 10y JGB ~1.7% + beta 1.1 x Japan ERP ~6.0% = ~8.3% cost of equity; the industrial business is net cash so WACC = cost of equity, rounded to 8.5% (house reference for JPY industrials is ~9%; Komatsu is a large-cap global #2 with an investment-grade balance sheet). Same 8.5% in all three scenarios: cyclicality, tariff and FX risk are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not in the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B): US GAAP ASC 842 operating lease cost is expensed inside EBITDA (SG&A/COGS), so operating lease liabilities (22,563 current + 55,959 long-term at Mar-26) are excluded from net debt. No separate lease_cost_pct_path needed because the segment-profit anchor is already post-lease-cost.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are 100% consolidated; noncontrolling interests deducted ONCE at book (196,263 at 30-Sep-2026, 6301.T_HalfYear_H1-2027.txt:526) in equity_bridge. NCI took 25,297 of 401,688 net income in FYE Mar-2026 (6.3%); book deduction of 196bn vs ~13x that profit share is the conservative end.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF on the INDUSTRIAL business (CMU + Industrial Machinery) plus a sum-of-parts bridge for the captive Retail Finance arm at book equity -- the dcf-methods routing row 'operating company, non-US or cyclical' with the embedded-lender adaptation. Reason: Komatsu reports under US GAAP with a 13-subsidiary captive finance business (RF assets 1,642.5bn, net D/E 4.50x) whose funding is 90% of consolidated interest-bearing debt. Folding it into an owner-FCF DCF would deduct 1.3tn of debt whose interest cost is already inside RF segment profit (segment COGS; reclassified below operating income in the 'Corporate & elimination' column) and would treat finance-receivable growth as working capital. CALIBRATION: FY0 industrial EBIT = CMU 491,118 + IM 37,937 = 529,055 (13.1% of 4,032,231); industrial D&A 133,815 (3.3%); industrial EBITDA 662,870 (16.4%); industrial cash capex ~188bn (consolidated 212,261 less RF 24,177) = 4.7%. Modelled FY0 NOPAT at 28% ~381bn vs attributable net income 376,391 -- ties within non-operating noise (RF profit after tax +26bn, equity income +10bn, NCI -25bn, net interest -28bn roughly offset). MID-CYCLE: CMU segment margin averaged 12.65% over FYE Mar-2019..Mar-2026 (14.7, 10.3, 7.3, 10.8, 13.5, 15.9, 15.8, 12.9); the FY0 12.9% and guided 12.2% CMU margins are mid-cycle, post-tariff, not peak -- so margins are NOT haircut further in the base; the peak the base case does normalise away is REVENUE, which sits on a JPY157-159/USD yen (JPY1/USD = JPY15.1bn sales, JPY4.6bn operating income per the filing's sensitivity) -- base growth fades to ~1% in Y3 and ~2.9% CAGR over 10 years against a 6.9%/yr nominal history since FY2015. TARIFFS: ~JPY25.8bn net FY (Komatsu FY2026) cost is already inside the guided 12.2% CMU margin that anchors Y1. CHINESE OEMs: addressed as a bull-margin ceiling (18% EBITDA, below the FY2024-25 ~19%) and in the bear margin path, not in WACC. TERMINAL: cap multiple 15x (base) / 16x (bull) / 12x (bear) owner FCF, per the method's 12-15x guidance for cyclicals; Gordon at 8.5%/2.0% is 15.7x so the cap binds in the base case. SBC: 0.03% of revenue, kept explicit; house and street coincide to within rounding, so band_position is not meaningful for this ticker.
inputs.cash_tax_note: Effective rate 27.1% (FYE Mar-2026, Japanese statutory 31.3%, foreign subsidiaries taxed lower; 6301.T_SecuritiesReport_FY2026.txt:1742); income taxes paid 179,022 on pre-tax 537,258 = 33% in FY0 reflects FY2025 peak accruals settling. 28% used throughout.
inputs.working_capital_note: Manufacturer: receivables + inventories (1,694.7bn at Sep-26, 42% of sales) far exceed payables (353.3bn), so growth consumes cash; wc_capture -20% of the revenue change (FY2021-26 cumulative OCF shortfall vs NI+D&A implies ~29% including Retail Finance receivables, which are excluded here).

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: mid-cycle trend. The 5-yr CAGRs (revenue 13.5%, EPS 29.8%, equity 12.9%) start from the COVID trough (FYE Mar-2021: revenue 2,189,512, EPS 112.39) and ride a JPY105->159/USD depreciation that adds ~680bn of translation gains to equity (AOCI). Nominal revenue CAGR since FYE Mar-2015 is 6.9%/yr; with the yen at a weak extreme and mining capex at a high, 3% is the trend rate the base case fades to.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5-yr CAGR (12.9%) diverges >30% from EPS 5-yr CAGR (29.8%): the EPS series is measured from a COVID trough and both are inflated by yen translation. Neither is a forward growth rate; see growth_rate_source.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF less SBC; SBC is only disclosed from FYE Mar-2024 and is <0.05% of revenue, so the adjustment is immaterial). FCF 3-yr CAGR is from a 22,941 trough (FYE Mar-2023 inventory rebuild) and is not meaningful. Consolidated reported FCF: FY2021 172,581; FY2022 138,014; FY2023 22,941; FY2024 231,831; FY2025 311,312; FY2026 236,702 (CSV labels = year ended 31 March). Period base for CAGRs: FY2026 vs FY2023 (3-yr) and FY2021 (5-yr).

base.growth_rationale: Y1 +8.0% vs guided industrial segment sales +8.2% (CMU 4,120bn + IM 257.5bn = 4,377.5bn against FY0 segment totals 4,044.8bn; the October 2026 raise embeds JPY159/USD in H1 and a conservative H2). Y2-Y3 fade to 3% and 1% as the FX tailwind lapses and coal-exposed Asian mining stays soft; Y4+ settle at 2-3% trend (aftermarket growth + ICT/AHS mix offsetting unit-share loss to XCMG/SANY at the value end). 10-yr CAGR ~2.9%.
base.margin_rationale: Y1 EBITDA 15.7% = guided CMU 12.2% / IM 17.1% EBIT (industrial 12.5%) + 3.3% D&A, i.e. the tariff-laden FY guidance. Drift to 16.2% (EBIT ~12.7%) as aftermarket/reman mix rises toward the +15% FY2027 plan target and Section-301 mitigation (pricing, sourcing) matures -- that is the 8-year CMU average (12.65%) plus a little mix, well below the FY2024-25 peak of ~19% EBITDA.
base.capex_rationale: Industrial cash capex ~4.7% of sales in FY0 (consolidated 212bn less RF 24bn) easing to 4.2% as the rental-fleet and reman (SRC Lexington) build normalises; D&A 3.3% rising to 3.5%. Terminal capex exceeds D&A by 0.7pp of sales, consistent with 2% nominal growth plus fleet renewal.

bull.rationale: Copper/gold capex cycle extends (AHS fleet 1,000 -> 1,200+ units, hard-rock sales to $400m), aftermarket reaches two-thirds of mining sales, the yen stays weak, and tariff mitigation plus pricing recover 2pp of margin; EBITDA margin 18% is still below the FY2024-25 peak (~19%). Terminal growth 2.5%, cap 16x.

bear.rationale: Y1 lands below guidance (+5%) as H2 yen strength bites; Y2-Y3 a mining-capex downturn (copper/gold correction joins the coal weakness already seen in Indonesia/Asia) plus a yen back toward 140 cut revenue 8% and 5% -- the FYE Mar-2020/2021 pattern -- with EBITDA margin to 12.0% (EBIT ~8.5%, between the FY2020 10.3% and FY2021 7.3% CMU margins). Partial recovery to 15.0% EBITDA, 0.7pp short of base because Chinese OEM price pressure and residual tariffs are structural. Terminal growth 1.5%, cap 12x.

scenario_narratives.base: Komatsu's axes are (1) the mining-capex cycle, half of CMU sales and bifurcated today between strong copper/gold (Latin America, Africa) and weak coal (Indonesia/Asia); (2) the yen, with ~90% of sales offshore at a JPY157-159/USD rate that flatters every JPY line; (3) US tariffs, ~JPY25.8bn net this year inside the guided 12.2% CMU margin; and (4) the aftermarket/AHS/ICT mix that is the defence against XCMG and SANY. Base: FY guidance delivered (+8% industrial sales, 15.7% EBITDA), then growth fades to ~1% by Y3 as the FX tailwind lapses, margins drift to the 8-year mid-cycle average plus a little mix (16.2% EBITDA / ~12.7% EBIT), capex eases toward 4.2% of sales. Retail Finance carried at book, net industrial cash and affiliates added, NCI and the pension deficit deducted.
scenario_narratives.bull: The copper/gold capex cycle runs for most of the decade (data-centre power, electrification), AHS passes 1,200 trucks and hard-rock mining reaches its $400m target, aftermarket climbs to two-thirds of mining sales, the yen stays weak, and tariff mitigation plus pricing restore ~2pp of margin -- 18% EBITDA, still below the FY2024-25 peak. Growth 10% then 6-3%; terminal growth 2.5%; 16x cap.
scenario_narratives.bear: Commodity prices correct in 2027-28 and the yen strengthens toward 140: industrial sales fall 8% then 5% (the FYE Mar-2020/21 shape), EBITDA margin troughs at 12% as volume deleverages against tariff and steel costs, and Chinese OEMs take the value end permanently, so the recovery stalls at 15% EBITDA. Retail Finance credit losses rise but it still stands at book; the industrial net-cash position is what keeps this a margin story rather than a solvency one. Terminal growth 1.5%; 12x cap.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised to 25% from the 15% house default: mining equipment is half of CMU, the revenue base sits on a historically weak yen, and tariff policy has moved between JPY25.8bn and JPY140bn of annual cost inside eighteen months. Bull cut to 25% from 35%: the bull case needs the commodity cycle, the yen and tariff relief to all cooperate. Base 50%: guidance has been raised, not cut, and the balance sheet (industrial net cash, 44% payout, JPY100bn/yr buybacks) carries no solvency axis, so the bear case is a margin downturn rather than distress -- which is why bear is 25% and not 35%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value the industrial equipment business on mid-cycle owner FCF and treat the captive Retail Finance arm as a separately-funded lender held at book, so that neither its JPY1.3tn of receivable-backed debt nor its receivable growth distorts the operating valuation. Margins are anchored to the tariff-laden FY guidance and the 8-year segment average, not to the FY2024-25 peak; the normalisation the base case imposes is on revenue (yen) and growth, not on margin. The cyclicality, FX and tariff risk live in the scenario paths and a 25% bear weight; the discount rate is a plain JPY cost of equity with no stacked premium.
key_risks_to_valuation: Yen: every JPY1/USD is ~JPY15.1bn of sales and ~JPY4.6bn of operating income; a move from 159 to 140 removes ~JPY85bn of EBIT (~15%) before any volume effect.
Mining capex cycle: copper/gold orders are the current support; a commodity correction would hit new equipment first and aftermarket with a lag.
US tariffs: estimates have swung JPY25.8bn to JPY140bn gross; Komatsu has ruled out major new US capacity, so the lever is pricing.
Chinese OEM price competition (XCMG, SANY) at the value end and in emerging markets; modelled as a margin ceiling, but share loss could also hit the growth path.
Retail Finance at book assumes credit losses and residual values stay benign; a 4.5x-levered captive is sensitive to a used-equipment price downturn.

Terminal cap multiple (15x owner FCF) binds in the base case; at 12x the base value falls materially, at 18x it rises -- the exit multiple is a judgment about what a buyer pays for a mid-cycle cyclical.
Working-capital capture (-20% of revenue change) is uncertain; Komatsu's FCF has lagged earnings for years and management is already behind the 3-year JPY1tn FCF target.
